mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% (over the past 3 months) signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in consumer and business demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) relative to the previous quarter's GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an impending economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion when INDPRO declines relative to GDPC1, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST > 1000) indicate robust consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% (over the past 3 months) signals rising inflation, which may lead to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the labor force (PAYEMS) grows at a rate below 0.5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.8%, it indicates a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth < 0.5% and UNRATE > 4.8%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-recession recovery regime, a sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105.0 signals accelerating economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances during post-recession recovery when INDPRO > 105.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
